title: EIP-8371: RowDAS - Distributed Blob Reconstruction
description: Distribute reconstruction load in the network through row-level cell messaging.
author: Csaba Kiraly (@cskiraly), Marco Munizaga (@MarcoPolo)
laymanDescription: Under PeerDAS each node holds a slice of every blob, so rebuilding missing data falls to supernodes that hold everything, and they all redo the same work. This proposal adds per-blob channels so different nodes rebuild different blobs, and ordinary nodes can help.
benefits: Supernode reconstruction load stops growing linearly with every added blob
A row's subnet members collectively cover enough columns to rebuild without any supernode
Makes blobs addressable by index, a prerequisite for rollups fetching only their own
tradeoffs: Adds gossip topics and bitmap signaling that need debouncing to avoid quadratic messages
Subnet assignment is a public function of node ID, so an attacker can grind IDs to eclipse one
Only peers whose libp2p supports cell-level deltas can participate
